waves.title: Who Owns UK Dentistry? The Groups, Their Backers, Their Size
waves.keywords: who owns mydentist, UK dental groups, dental group acquisitions UK, dental corporates UK, private equity dentistry UK, largest dental groups UK
waves.brief: The flagship: the seed article for the UK Dental Deals and Groups Tracker, and the title's clearest statement of its seam (the practice as an asset). UK practice sales and group acquisitions do not reach Google News, so no publisher holds a structured answer to 'who owns which dental group'; Dental Group Signal writes essays, not a ledger. Write the reference for a practice OWNER deciding whether to sell, stay independent or partner with a group, and for the advisers around that decision. Structure: how much of UK dentistry the groups actually own (a minority, and why that matters for sellers), then a table of the largest groups with owner or sponsor, the date the current owner bought in, and practice count where published, each row carrying its dated source in the row itself, then what buyers are paying for and why NHS and mixed practices are back in demand. Close with what consolidation means for an independent owner: more bidders, a benchmark for their own valuation, and the questions to ask any group buyer. Never estimate a practice count or a deal value in our own voice; a blank beats a guess, because this table becomes a tracker and one invented row poisons it. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026; attribute in text exactly): Christie & Co's Dental Market Review 2026, as reported by Dentistry.co.uk on 10 Sep 2026, found only 19% of UK practices are owned by corporate and large-group operators, and around 8,000 of the UK's roughly 12,000 practices are independent single or dual-site operators; the same report says corporate DSOs are showing renewed interest in acquiring NHS and mixed practices. Bridgepoint completed its acquisition of mydentist from Palamon Capital Partners in October 2025; the enterprise value was REPORTED at £750m to £800m and Palamon reported a 3.0x return (attribute both as reported, never as fact); mydentist describes itself as operating more than 500 practices; CEO Nilesh Pandya stayed invested. LaingBuisson's Dentistry UK Market Report (7th edition, September 2025) credits private equity-backed groups with leading consolidation. For every other group in the table (Bupa Dental Care, PortmanDentex, Rodericks, Colosseum Dental UK, Clyde Munro, Together Dental, European Dental Group), use only the group's own current website or a dated press release for size and owner; if a count cannot be sourced, leave the cell reading 'not published'. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'dental group' in the first paragraph; the table is the centre of the piece; link out to every group and to Christie & Co. Owner rule applies: nothing for patients.

waves.title: UDA Values in 2026: How the NHS Dental Contract Pays Practices
waves.keywords: UDA value 2026, NHS dental contract explained, units of dental activity, minimum UDA rate, NHS dental contract changes April 2026, unscheduled care dental contract
waves.brief: The measured SERP gap: 'UDA value 2026 NHS dental contract explained' is held by a tutoring blog, NHS England's own guidance, the BDA and two AI-written vendor blogs. No publisher ranks. Write the owner's explainer: how an NHS practice in England is actually paid in 2026/27, written for the principal and practice manager who have to deliver the contract, not for patients. Structure: what a UDA is and how contract value (NACV) works; why UDA values differ between practices and what the minimum rate does; the April 2026 changes and exactly what they cost or earn a practice (the unscheduled care requirement worked through as an example for a practice with a 20,000 pound NACV, using the NHS England formula below); clawback and the end-of-year reconciliation; and what the reforms have NOT changed. Then the live politics in one tight section: the ADG and BDA positions, attributed. A short box on the three devolved regimes, pointing out that Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland run different contracts. Never assert a typical UDA value in our voice; ranges only, attributed. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): NHS England's 2026/27 confirmation: providers with mandatory services contracts of 100 UDAs or more must deliver 8.2% of contract value as unscheduled care, which equals 11 courses of treatment per £10,000 of NACV, credited as a £15 fixed credit per required course plus a £60 activity credit per delivered course. The minimum UDA rate of £28 was set by NHS England in 2024. On 17 Sep 2026 the BDA rejected the Association of Dental Groups' call for incremental reform as BDA leaders met James Frith, the minister responsible for dentistry, at DHSC (reported by Dentistry.co.uk); the ADG had asked for the April changes to be evaluated before further incremental reform, a review of the minimum UDA rate, and exploration of a separate children's contract. A BDA survey of dentists in England found 1% expected to increase NHS work after the changes, 63% expected to reduce it and 10% believed the changes had improved NHS dentistry. Northern Ireland's Department of Health published its General Dental Services Cost of Service Review on 16 Sep 2026. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'UDA' and '2026' in the first paragraph; one worked example with the arithmetic shown; link to NHS England's guidance and to the BDA's contract pages.

waves.title: What Is a Dental Practice Worth? How UK Valuations Work in 2026
waves.keywords: dental practice valuation UK, how much is my dental practice worth, dental practice goodwill value, dental practice EBITDA multiple, selling dental practice price
waves.brief: The single most winnable owner query measured: 'dental practice valuation UK' is held entirely by brokers (Samera, Dental Elite, PFM Dental, Eclipse) and US brokers. No publisher ranks. Write the neutral explainer an owner reads before they phone a broker. Structure: the two ways practices are valued (goodwill plus assets, and a multiple of adjusted profit or EBITDA) and when each is used; what moves the number (NHS versus private versus mixed income, UDA value and contract security, associate dependence, lease length, freehold, CQC standing, patient list and plan membership); why a group buyer and an individual buyer pay differently; and the current market read. Close with the owner's checklist before instructing a valuer, and a note that NASDAL members and specialist brokers are where to go next. Multiples are the trap: the brief records a 6.5x to 9.5x EBITDA range from a broker blog as unverified, so never state a multiple unless it is attributed to a named, dated source you can link; otherwise describe the method, not a number. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): Christie & Co's Dental Market Review 2026 (reported by Dentistry.co.uk, 10 Sep 2026): average asset prices rose 2.9% in 2025 after a 9.6% fall in 2024; 57% of accepted offers for practice sales were at or above asking price, of which 45% were above; demand for high-quality practices is outstripping supply. NASDAL's 2025 benchmarking (compiled by Humphrey & Co from 650 principals and limited companies, reported 1 May 2026): average net profit per principal was £198,291 private, £196,559 NHS and £193,532 mixed; wages and direct costs rose to 47% of fee income from 45.8%. NASDAL also runs a Goodwill Survey (its own feed, Sep 2026); cite it only by linking the NASDAL page. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'dental practice valuation' in the first paragraph; a table of value drivers with the direction each moves the price; no broker named as 'best'.

waves.title: UK Dentistry in 2026: A £12bn Market Going Private
waves.keywords: UK dental market size, UK dentistry market 2026, private dentistry growth UK, dental market statistics UK, NHS dentistry spending
waves.brief: The title's position piece: what this publication is for, told through the numbers. The £12bn figure, the private shift, the profits recovering and the consolidators buying: each is a business story that lands on an independent owner. Report the data with strict attribution and do the analysis nobody else does: what it means for a practice owner's next decision (stay NHS, go mixed, convert, sell). Structure: market size and the private share; profits; prices and deals; workforce; and the NHS contract fight. Each section ends with the owner consequence in one plain sentence. The figure rule is load-bearing here: LaingBuisson's value is the high-street market; never blend it with the NHS dental budget or with practice income, and name source and year on every figure. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): LaingBuisson Dentistry UK Market Report, 7th edition (published 11 Sep 2025): UK high-street dentistry worth £12.16bn in 2023/24, up 9.2%; private-pay £8.4bn, 69%, the highest share since LaingBuisson began reporting; NHS-funded £3.78bn. Christie & Co Dental Market Review 2026 (via Dentistry.co.uk, 10 Sep 2026): 19% of practices owned by corporates and large groups; around 8,000 of about 12,000 practices independent; average asset prices +2.9% in 2025 after -9.6% in 2024; vacancy rates 19% in NHS dentistry and 15% in private. NASDAL 2025 benchmarking: net profit per principal £198,291 private, £196,559 NHS, £193,532 mixed. Official Dental Earnings and Expenses Estimates 2024/25 (published 30 Jul 2026): average taxable income for self-employed dentists in England rose 6.1% to £83,000. GDC register at December 2025: 131,680 registrants, 47,916 dentists. BDA survey (Sep 2026): 63% of dentists expect to reduce NHS work. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'UK dental market' in the first paragraph; a one-table summary of the headline numbers with source and year in every row. Never present the private shift as good or bad news in our voice; present it as the decision in front of the owner.

waves.brief: The measured SERP is Capterra, Slashdot, SoftwareSuggest, an AI-written vendor blog and two vendors. A neutral buyer's guide written by a publisher would be the only independent voice. Write for the owner or practice manager choosing or switching a system. Structure: what the software actually has to do in a UK practice (appointments, charting, NHS claims and UDA tracking, plan membership and direct debits, patient finance, recalls and reminders, reporting, CQC evidence); cloud versus server; switching cost and data migration (the real reason practices stay put); then a comparison table of the main UK systems with deployment model, NHS claims support and pricing model, each cell taken only from the vendor's own current site (write 'not published' where it is not). Close with the ten questions to ask on a demo. Name real vendors (Software of Excellence EXACT, Dentally, Carestream CS R4+, iSmile, Kiroku, Clero and any others you can source) and describe, never rank; confirm corporate ownership of each product from the vendor's own site before stating it. The scope rule applies: clinical charting features are described as practice-workflow features, never as clinical recommendations. waves.title: CQC Dental Inspections in 2026: What Owners Need Ready
waves.keywords: CQC dental inspection checklist 2026, CQC dental practice inspection, CQC registration dental practice, dental compliance CQC, CQC new assessment framework dental
waves.brief: Measured SERP: compliance vendors (GoAudits, Lumiform, Agilio, Radar) and an AI farm, with CQC itself. No publisher. Write the owner's and practice manager's guide to being inspected in 2026, which is a moving target because CQC is replacing its single assessment framework. Structure: what is changing and when; the five key questions and what evidence an inspector asks for under each in a dental setting (policies, infection control records, radiography, medical emergencies, safeguarding, staff files and DBS, complaints, governance); the registered manager's responsibilities; what happens after a poor rating, as process only. Close with a practical readiness list. The fitness-to-practise rule applies absolutely: no named practice, no named individual, no example drawn from a live case; use only CQC's own published guidance. Compliance vendors are named as a category with links, never recommended. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): two independent reviews criticised CQC's Single Assessment Framework; CQC is replacing it with four sector-specific frameworks by the end of 2026, of which the primary care and community services framework covers dental practices; key lines of enquiry return in place of quality statements; CQC's consultation on the draft frameworks closed on 12 June 2026. Phrase the timetable as CQC's stated plan, not as done, and tell the reader to check CQC's current guidance before an inspection. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'CQC' and 'dental' in the first paragraph; link to CQC's own dental guidance pages.

waves.title: Leaving the NHS: The Real Numbers Behind Going Private
waves.keywords: converting NHS dental practice to private, going private dental practice, leaving NHS dentistry, NHS to private dentistry, handing back NHS dental contract
waves.brief: The seed piece for the Private Conversion Index. The SERP is held by FMC and a plan provider, so we do not win it with another how-to; we win it with numbers the others do not assemble. Write for the principal weighing conversion. Structure: the scale of the shift (market share, dentist intentions); the economics of the decision (what an NHS contract pays, what private income replaces it, the patient-retention risk, plan membership as the bridge); the mechanics (contract notice, the commissioner, what happens to NHS patients, communicating with the list); and what the NHSBSA contract data will let this title track by area over time (say plainly that the tracker is coming, and what it will measure). Every economic claim is an attributed range; never promise an income. The owner rule: no patient advice, no 'how to find an NHS dentist'. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026): LaingBuisson (Sep 2025): private-pay dentistry reached £8.4bn, 69% of a £12.16bn high-street market in 2023/24, a record share. BDA survey (reported 17 Sep 2026): 1% of dentists in England expect to increase NHS work after the April 2026 changes, 63% expect to reduce it. NASDAL 2025: private practice profit per principal rose to £198,291 from £161,910 in 2024, and NHS practice profit to £196,559 from £165,871; state the near-parity plainly, because it undercuts the lazy assumption that private is automatically more profitable. Christie & Co 2026: DSOs show renewed interest in buying NHS and mixed practices. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'going private' and 'NHS contract' in the first paragraph; a table comparing the NHS, mixed and private models on income source, risk and profit per principal (NASDAL figures only).

waves.title: Dental Nurse Visas Fell 95%: How Practices Are Recruiting Now
waves.keywords: dental nurse shortage UK 2026, dental nurse visa sponsorship, skilled worker visa dental nurse, recruiting dental nurses UK, dental workforce shortage
waves.brief: The SERP is recruiter-held (BritAsia and others) and a law firm. The news hook is the visa collapse; the evergreen value is the owner's recruiting playbook. Write for the practice owner or manager with a nursing gap. Structure: what changed on 22 July 2025 and who it affects (nurses, hygienists and technicians off the route; therapists still eligible); what the Home Office figures show and, as importantly, what they do not; the transitional rules for staff already sponsored (process only, point to Home Office guidance and regulated advice); then the domestic options: trainee nurses and apprenticeships, retention and pay, skill mix with therapists, and the GDC register growth that partly offsets the loss. Never give immigration advice in our voice. SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026; Dentistry.co.uk, 14 Sep 2026, citing Home Office figures): the rule changes published 1 July 2025 took effect on 22 July 2025 and raised the skilled worker threshold to RQF level 6; there were six sponsored work entry-clearance grants for dental nurses in Q4 2025 to Q2 2026 against 122 in the previous three quarters, a fall of about 95%; these are main applicants from outside the UK only and exclude in-country extensions and switches; DHSC confirmed in a corrected parliamentary answer that dental therapists meet RQF 6 and remain eligible for the Health and Care Worker visa. GDC register at December 2025: 68,472 dental nurses (up 5.4%), 8,661 dental therapists (up 21%), 11,292 hygienists (up 11%). Christie & Co 2026: vacancy rates of 19% in NHS and 15% in private dentistry. STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS: 'dental nurse' in the first paragraph; state explicitly that the 95% fall is in one visa route, not in the workforce.

waves.title: Dental Practice Openings and Closures: Where Capacity Is Moving

waves.brief: The seed piece for the Practice Openings and Closures Tracker, and the strongest format signal measured across our titles, applied to dentistry: named openings and closures, each a named local business that may share the story. Write it as analysis of capacity for owners and investors, never as a patient access story. Structure: why openings and closures matter to an owner (local competition, patient flow, acquisition targets, recruitment pools); what the September 2026 wire shows, as a dated list of named openings and closures, each linking to its source; the pattern behind them (NHS contract handbacks, private openings, group relocations and mergers); and how this title will track them from CQC registrations going forward. Only include a practice where a named, dated source reports it; never infer a closure. Access-crisis framing enters only as contract economics and capacity (the owner rule). SOURCE ANCHORS (pre-verified 18 Sep 2026, from the wire): a new dental practice opened in Rotherham after a £2.1m investment (Rotherham Advertiser, 11 Sep 2026); a new practice at Bodlondeb, Conwy was reported as set to open soon (North Wales Pioneer, 18 Sep 2026); 5,000 new NHS dental places opened across three Lancashire towns (Lancashire Telegraph, 17 Sep 2026); plans were submitted for a dental practice in another Powys town as a group expands (County Times, 13 Sep 2026); a dental group expansion into south Wales by acquisition was reported (Caerphilly Observer, 10 Sep 2026). Re-read each source before using it and use the practice and group names exactly as the source prints them.
